design: Entry=line0, body=line2. Major sections H/B/P/S/T are held out one at a time. Training excludes the held-out section entirely. Source paragraphs require >=5 usable tokens at both endpoints. Evaluation compares nuisance-only, frozen 60B carrier, and broader structural models.

models.nuisance: token count, TTR, mean length, length SD, character inventory, character entropy
models.carrier: 60B stable carrier set: TTR, mean length, edit1 fraction, local previous-10 continuity, k/t mass, k-share, first entropy, last entropy
models.structural: carrier plus broader edge/prefix/suffix and structural features; token count excluded

decision: P60-3 survives. A section-blind structural entry role transfers to every held-out major section. Simple length/frequency nuisance features already contain real entry information, but the broader structural model adds a positive paired entry-vs-body probability margin beyond that nuisance baseline in all five sections; page-cluster bootstrap intervals for the incremental margin are above zero in every section. Multiple prefix/suffix and k/t-related coefficient directions are invariant across all five outer held-out-section fits.
qualification: The frozen 60B carrier-only model is not uniformly superior to nuisance-only, especially in Biological and Stars. The support comes from the broader transferable structural role, not from claiming the 60B carrier set alone is sufficient. Prefix/suffix features are EVA formal units, not semantic morphemes.
interpretation: Paragraph entry is not merely a section-specific formatting accident. Across H/B/P/S/T, entry lines share a transferable formal signature: longer/more diverse surface forms, reduced k/t-family mass and several stable edge-pattern shifts relative to line2 body state. This supports a manuscript-wide formal entry role while remaining agnostic about whether that role encodes headings, item initialization, cipher state, or formal pseudo-text machinery.
next: Phase60D prospective recovery: test whether the structural composition of an entry line predicts the direction/magnitude of its own paragraph's later body state beyond page/section baselines on held-out leaves.
